target_customer: Pharma companies buying AI drug discovery software, later its own oncology pipeline partners
problem: Drug discovery for kinase targets is slow and expensive; Reverie used machine learning to predict molecule properties and speed up design of brain-penetrant cancer therapies.
business_model: Software and collaboration deals with pharma, then an internal drug pipeline

founders.name: Ankit Gupta
founders.background_notes: YC page: ML researcher who moved into infrastructure and full stack work; later joined Ginkgo as Head of AI/ML Advancement and became a YC General Partner.

founders.name: Jonah Kallenbach
founders.background_notes: Harvard SEAS alumni news names him and Gupta as founders.

founders.name: Connor Duffy
founders.background_notes: Listed as founder on the YC page with no background.

exit.reason: Ginkgo acquired key assets (platform and AI team), not the whole company; terms not disclosed.

technical_complexity.rationale: Predicting kinase inhibitor properties with ML and designing brain-penetrant molecules needed chemistry, ML and CRO coordination.

defensibility.rationale: Proprietary models and pipeline data helped, but computational drug discovery was crowded and results needed clinical proof.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Ginkgo bought key assets in February 2024.

market_need_then: Pharma was increasingly partnering with ML drug discovery firms; Reverie later signed a collaboration with Roche and Genentech in July 2020.

brand_strength.rationale: No press about the brand was found; many unrelated companies use Reverie as a name.

pivots.to: own drug pipeline of brain-penetrant cancer therapies using its ML tools
pivots.why: YC page says it began with software for pharma then built its own pipeline; the exact date is not stated.

outcome_analysis: Reverie raised a 25 million dollar Series A in February 2021 and built a virtual oncology pipeline, but by February 2024 Ginkgo bought only its platform and AI team. Sources do not state the cause; the failure factors reflect the asset sale and the 2022 to 2024 biotech funding downturn and are an inference.
notes: reverielabs.com returned HTTP 503. VentureBeat says the Series A brought total raised to over 32 million dollars, so about 7 million of earlier funding is partly accounted for by the 6.6 million 2020 round, whose attribution rests on a single database listing (the search summary did not name which database, so the source_url is the CB Insights page and is unverified). The seed amount is unknown; one aggregator lists 120k. Competitors: a search for AI drug discovery peers found only undated or later lists, so none are recorded with a source dated near the batch.
